claim: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal disease affecting >20 million people worldwide.
source: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal disease affecting >20 million people worldwide.
evidence: This is a statement of prevalence presented in the abstract without supporting data in the manuscript itself, but is presented as established knowledge.

claim: Loss of daylight vision in RP typically occurs due to the dysfunction/loss of cone photoreceptors.
source: Loss of daylight vision typically occurs due to the dysfunction/loss of cone photoreceptors, the cell type that initiates our color and high-acuity vision.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the mechanism of vision loss in RP.

claim: Cone photoreceptors are the cell type that initiates color and high-acuity vision.
source: Loss of daylight vision typically occurs due to the dysfunction/loss of cone photoreceptors, the cell type that initiates our color and high-acuity vision.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about cone photoreceptor function.

claim: Currently, there is no effective treatment for RP, other than gene therapy for a limited number of specific disease genes.
source: Currently, there is no effective treatment for RP, other than gene therapy for a limited number of specific disease genes.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the current state of RP treatment.

claim: 20 genes were screened for their ability to prolong cone photoreceptor survival in vivo.
source: To develop a disease gene-agnostic therapy, we screened 20 genes for their ability to prolong cone photoreceptor survival in vivo.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study, supported by data in Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: An adeno-associated virus vector expressing Txnip prolongs the survival of cone photoreceptors in RP mouse models.
source: Here, we report an adeno-associated virus vector expressing Txnip, which prolongs the survival of cone photoreceptors and improves visual acuity in RP mouse models.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: An adeno-associated virus vector expressing Txnip improves visual acuity in RP mouse models.
source: Here, we report an adeno-associated virus vector expressing Txnip, which prolongs the survival of cone photoreceptors and improves visual acuity in RP mouse models.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A Txnip allele, C247S, which blocks the association of Txnip with thioredoxin, provides an even greater benefit than wildtype Txnip for cone survival.
source: A Txnip allele, C247S, which blocks the association of Txnip with thioredoxin, provides an even greater benefit.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, and the functional property of C247S is cited to Patwari et al., 2006.

claim: The rescue effect of Txnip depends on lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb).
source: Additionally, the rescue effect of Txnip depends on lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb) and correlates with the presence of healthier mitochondria, suggesting that Txnip saves RP cones by enhancing their lactate catabolism.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The rescue effect of Txnip correlates with the presence of healthier mitochondria.
source: Additionally, the rescue effect of Txnip depends on lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb) and correlates with the presence of healthier mitochondria, suggesting that Txnip saves RP cones by enhancing their lactate catabolism.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Txnip saves RP cones by enhancing their lactate catabolism.
source: Additionally, the rescue effect of Txnip depends on lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb) and correlates with the presence of healthier mitochondria, suggesting that Txnip saves RP cones by enhancing their lactate catabolism.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the experimental findings with Ldhb and lactate utilization.

claim: Retinitis pigmentosa affects approximately 1 in ~4,000 people.
source: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is one of the most prevalent types of inherited retinal diseases affecting approximately 1 in ~4,000 people (Hartong et al., 2006).
evidence: This prevalence estimate is supported by citation to Hartong et al., 2006.

claim: In RP, the rod photoreceptors are primarily affected by the disease genes and degenerate first.
source: In RP, the rod photoreceptors, which initiate night vision, are primarily affected by the disease genes and degenerate first.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the progression of RP.

claim: The degeneration of cones follows the degeneration of rods in RP.
source: The degeneration of cones, the photoreceptors that initiate daylight, color, and high-acuity vision, then follows, which greatly impacts the quality of life.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the progression of RP.

claim: Gene therapy using adeno-associated virus (AAV) holds great promise for RP.
source: Currently, one therapy that holds great promise for RP is gene therapy using adeno-associated virus (AAV) (Maguire et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maguire et al., 2019.

claim: AAV gene therapy has proven successful for a small number of genes affecting a few disease families.
source: This approach has proven successful for a small number of genes affecting a few disease families (Cehajic-Kapetanovic et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cehajic-Kapetanovic et al., 2020.

claim: There are approximately 100 RP disease genes that primarily affect rods.
source: However, due to the number and functional heterogeneity of RP disease genes (≈100 genes that primarily affect rods, https://sph.uth.edu/retnet/), gene therapy for each RP gene will be logistically and financially difficult.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge with reference to a database (retnet).

claim: Gene therapy for each RP gene will be logistically and financially difficult due to the number and functional heterogeneity of RP disease genes.
source: However, due to the number and functional heterogeneity of RP disease genes (≈100 genes that primarily affect rods, https://sph.uth.edu/retnet/), gene therapy for each RP gene will be logistically and financially difficult.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the large number of disease genes.

claim: A considerable number of RP patients do not have an identified disease gene.
source: In addition, a considerable number of RP patients do not have an identified disease gene.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about RP patient populations.

claim: The disease gene in RP is typically not expressed in cones.
source: Given that the disease gene is typically not expressed in cones, and thus their death is due to non-autonomous mechanisms that may be in common across affected families, answers to the question of why cones die may provide an avenue to a widely applicable therapy for RP.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about RP disease mechanisms.

claim: Cone death in RP is due to non-autonomous mechanisms that may be in common across affected families.
source: Given that the disease gene is typically not expressed in cones, and thus their death is due to non-autonomous mechanisms that may be in common across affected families, answers to the question of why cones die may provide an avenue to a widely applicable therapy for RP.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the fact that disease genes are not expressed in cones.

claim: Oxidative damage is a suggested mechanism of cone death in RP.
source: To date, the suggested mechanisms of cone death include oxidative damage (Komeima et al., 2006; Wellard et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2015), inflammation (Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2015), and a shortage of nutrients (Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Kanow et al., 2017; Punzo et al., 2012; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Komeima et al., 2006; Wellard et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2015.

claim: Inflammation is a suggested mechanism of cone death in RP.
source: To date, the suggested mechanisms of cone death include oxidative damage (Komeima et al., 2006; Wellard et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2015), inflammation (Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2015), and a shortage of nutrients (Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Kanow et al., 2017; Punzo et al., 2012; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: A shortage of nutrients is a suggested mechanism of cone death in RP.
source: To date, the suggested mechanisms of cone death include oxidative damage (Komeima et al., 2006; Wellard et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2015), inflammation (Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2015), and a shortage of nutrients (Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Kanow et al., 2017; Punzo et al., 2012; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Kanow et al., 2017; Punzo et al., 2012; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016.

claim: In 2009, gene expression changes during retinal degeneration were surveyed in four mouse models of RP.
source: In 2009, we surveyed gene expression changes that occurred during retinal degeneration in four mouse models of RP (Punzo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Punzo et al., 2009.

claim: Cones starve and die due to a shortage of glucose in RP.
source: Those data led us to suggest a model wherein cones starve and die due to a shortage of glucose, which is typically used for energy and anabolic needs in photoreceptors via glycolysis.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on gene expression data from Punzo et al., 2009.

claim: Evidence of the 'glucose shortage hypothesis' was provided by orthogonal approaches from other groups.
source: Evidence of this 'glucose shortage hypothesis' was subsequently provided by orthogonal approaches from other groups (Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016.

claim: Only Txnip had a beneficial effect on cone survival among 20 genes tested in three mouse models of RP.
source: These studies have inspired us to test 20 genes that might affect the uptake and/or utilization of glucose by cones in vivo in three mouse models of RP (Figure 1—source data 1). Only one gene, Txnip, had a beneficial effect, prolonging cone survival and visual acuity in these models.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Txnip encodes an α-arrestin family member protein with multiple functions.
source: Txnip encodes an α-arrestin family member protein with multiple functions, including binding to thioredoxin (Junn et al., 2000; Nishiyama et al., 1999), facilitating removal of the glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) from the cell membrane (Wu et al., 2013), and promoting the use of non-glucose fuels (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies describing Txnip functions.

claim: Txnip binds to thioredoxin.
source: Txnip encodes an α-arrestin family member protein with multiple functions, including binding to thioredoxin (Junn et al., 2000; Nishiyama et al., 1999), facilitating removal of the glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) from the cell membrane (Wu et al., 2013), and promoting the use of non-glucose fuels (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Junn et al., 2000; Nishiyama et al., 1999.

claim: Txnip facilitates removal of GLUT1 from the cell membrane.
source: Txnip encodes an α-arrestin family member protein with multiple functions, including binding to thioredoxin (Junn et al., 2000; Nishiyama et al., 1999), facilitating removal of the glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) from the cell membrane (Wu et al., 2013), and promoting the use of non-glucose fuels (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2013.

claim: Txnip promotes the use of non-glucose fuels.
source: Txnip encodes an α-arrestin family member protein with multiple functions, including binding to thioredoxin (Junn et al., 2000; Nishiyama et al., 1999), facilitating removal of the glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) from the cell membrane (Wu et al., 2013), and promoting the use of non-glucose fuels (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to DeBalsi et al., 2014.

claim: α-arrestins are structurally distinct from visual or β-arrestins.
source: Because α-arrestins are structurally distinct from the visual or β-arrestins, such as ARR3, Txnip is unlikely to bind to opsins or to participate in phototransduction (Hwang et al., 2014; Kang et al., 2015; Puca and Brou, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hwang et al., 2014; Kang et al., 2015; Puca and Brou, 2014.

claim: Txnip is unlikely to bind to opsins or to participate in phototransduction.
source: Because α-arrestins are structurally distinct from the visual or β-arrestins, such as ARR3, Txnip is unlikely to bind to opsins or to participate in phototransduction (Hwang et al., 2014; Kang et al., 2015; Puca and Brou, 2014).
evidence: This is a logical inference based on structural differences, supported by citations.

claim: The C247S mutation in Txnip blocks the association of Txnip with thioredoxin.
source: We tested a number of Txnip alleles and found that one allele, C247S, which blocks the association of Txnip with thioredoxin (Patwari et al., 2006), provided the greatest benefit.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Patwari et al., 2006.

claim: Investigation of the mechanism of Txnip rescue revealed that it required lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb).
source: Investigation of the mechanism of Txnip rescue revealed that it required lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb), which catalyzes the conversion of lactate to pyruvate.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ldhb catalyzes the conversion of lactate to pyruvate.
source: Investigation of the mechanism of Txnip rescue revealed that it required lactate dehydrogenase b (Ldhb), which catalyzes the conversion of lactate to pyruvate.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about Ldhb function.

claim: Imaging of metabolic reporters demonstrated an enhanced intracellular ATP:ADP ratio when the retina was placed in lactate medium.
source: Imaging of metabolic reporters demonstrated an enhanced intracellular ATP:ADP ratio when the retina was placed in lactate medium.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mitochondria appeared to be healthier as a result of Txnip addition.
source: Moreover, by several measures, mitochondria appeared to be healthier as a result of Txnip addition, but this improvement was not sufficient for cone rescue.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Improved mitochondrial health by Txnip was not sufficient for cone rescue.
source: Moreover, by several measures, mitochondria appeared to be healthier as a result of Txnip addition, but this improvement was not sufficient for cone rescue.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data, particularly with Txnip.S308A and Parp1 knockout experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Txnip shifts cones from their normal reliance on glucose to enhanced utilization of lactate.
source: The above observations led to a model wherein Txnip shifts cones from their normal reliance on glucose to enhanced utilization of lactate, as well as marked improvement in mitochondrial structure and function.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: Txnip leads to marked improvement in mitochondrial structure and function.
source: The above observations led to a model wherein Txnip shifts cones from their normal reliance on glucose to enhanced utilization of lactate, as well as marked improvement in mitochondrial structure and function.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Txnip in combination with anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative damage genes showed additive benefits for cones.
source: Finally, as our goal is to rescue cones that suffer not only from metabolic challenges, but also from inflammation and oxidative damage, we tested Txnip in combination with anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative damage genes, and found additive benefits for cones.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: These treatments may benefit cones not only in RP, but also in other ocular diseases where similar environmental stresses are present, such as in age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
source: These treatments may benefit cones not only in RP, but also in other ocular diseases where similar environmental stresses are present, such as in age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential broader applications.

claim: AAV-RedO-Txnip prolonged cone survival at P50 in rd1 mice compared to control.
source: Among the vectors with individual or combinations of genes, only Txnip preserved rd1 cones at P50 (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: Txnip did not change the number of cones at P20 prior to their death in rd1 mice.
source: The effects were likely on cone survival as it did not change the number of cones at P20 prior to their death, but did provide survival benefit by ~P30 (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Txnip provided survival benefit by ~P30 in rd1 mice.
source: The effects were likely on cone survival as it did not change the number of cones at P20 prior to their death, but did provide survival benefit by ~P30 (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The level of Txnip rescue in P50 rd1 cones was comparable to that seen using AAV with a CMV promoter to express Nrf2.
source: The level of Txnip rescue in P50 rd1 cones was comparable to that seen using AAV with a cytomegalovirus (CMV) promoter to express a transcription factor, Nrf2, that regulates anti-oxidation pathways and reduces inflammation, as we found previously (Xiong et al., 2015; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and citation to Xiong et al., 2015.

claim: Nrf2 regulates anti-oxidation pathways and reduces inflammation.
source: The level of Txnip rescue in P50 rd1 cones was comparable to that seen using AAV with a cytomegalovirus (CMV) promoter to express a transcription factor, Nrf2, that regulates anti-oxidation pathways and reduces inflammation, as we found previously (Xiong et al., 2015; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xiong et al., 2015.

claim: The combination of Hk1 plus Pfkm led to a reduction in cone survival.
source: One combination led to a reduction in cone survival, that of Hk1 plus Pfkm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Txnip improved cone survival in rd10 mice at P130.
source: Both rd10 and Rho-/- mice showed improved cone survival (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: Txnip improved cone survival in Rho-/- mice at P150.
source: Both rd10 and Rho-/- mice showed improved cone survival (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: The rescue effect of Txnip did not persist long term, as by P240 in the Rho-/- strain it was not significant.
source: The rescue effect did not persist long term, however, as by P240 in the Rho-/- strain it was not significant (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Txnip-transduced eyes showed enhanced visual acuity compared to control contralateral eyes in rd10 mice.
source: Under conditions that simulated daylight, Txnip-transduced eyes showed enhanced visual acuity compared to the control contralateral eyes in rd10 and Rho-/- mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Txnip-transduced eyes showed enhanced visual acuity compared to control contralateral eyes in Rho-/- mice.
source: Under conditions that simulated daylight, Txnip-transduced eyes showed enhanced visual acuity compared to the control contralateral eyes in rd10 and Rho-/- mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No effect on ERG was observed in rd10 mice transduced with Txnip.
source: To determine if there was an improvement in overall cone phototransduction, summed across all cones, electroretinography (ERG) was carried out. No effect was observed in rd10 mice transduced with Txnip (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Txnip had no effect on PNA staining in wildtype mice.
source: Txnip also was evaluated for effects on cones in wildtype (WT) mice using peanut agglutinin (PNA) staining, which stains the cone-specific extracellular matrix and reflects cone health. No effect was seen on PNA staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: At P31, the approximate number and morphology of Txnip-transduced cones in WT retinas was similar to uninfected WT retinas.
source: In addition, retinas from both WT and P21 rd1 mice were stained using anti-ARR3, which stains the entire cone. At P31, the approximate number and morphology of Txnip-transduced cones in WT retinas was similar to uninfected WT retinas (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: IHC for ARR3 in rd1 retinas at P21 and P30 did not show an obvious rescue of cone outer segments by Txnip.
source: At P21 and P30, immunohistochemistry (IHC) for ARR3 in rd1 retinas did not show an obvious rescue of cone outer segments by Txnip (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The C247S mutation in Txnip blocks Txnip's inhibitory interaction with thioredoxin.
source: A C247S mutation has been shown to block Txnip's inhibitory interaction with thioredoxin (Patwari et al., 2009; Patwari et al., 2006), which is an important component of a cell's ability to fight oxidative damage via thiol groups (Junn et al., 2000; Nishinaka et al., 2001; Nishiyama et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Patwari et al., 2009; Patwari et al., 2006.

claim: Thioredoxin is an important component of a cell's ability to fight oxidative damage via thiol groups.
source: A C247S mutation has been shown to block Txnip's inhibitory interaction with thioredoxin (Patwari et al., 2009; Patwari et al., 2006), which is an important component of a cell's ability to fight oxidative damage via thiol groups (Junn et al., 2000; Nishinaka et al., 2001; Nishiyama et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Junn et al., 2000; Nishinaka et al., 2001; Nishiyama et al., 1999.

claim: The C247S allele provided more robust cone rescue than WT Txnip in all three RP mouse strains.
source: The C247S clearly provided more robust cone rescue than WT Txnip in all three RP mouse strains (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: The therapeutic effect of Txnip does not require an inhibitory interaction with thioredoxins.
source: These results indicate that the therapeutic effect of Txnip does not require an inhibitory interaction with thioredoxins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that C247S, which cannot bind thioredoxin, provides better rescue than WT Txnip.

claim: Anti-oxidation strategies promoted cone survival in RP mice.
source: This finding is in keeping with previous work, which showed that anti-oxidation strategies promoted cone survival in RP mice (Komeima et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2021; Xiong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Komeima et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2021; Xiong et al., 2015.

claim: The S308A change did not benefit cone survival in either the WT Txnip or C247S context.
source: An additional mutation, S308A, which loses an AMPK/Akt-phosphorylation site on Txnip (Waldhart et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2013), was tested in the context of WT Txnip and in the context of the C247S allele. The S308A change did not benefit cone survival in either context (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and citations to Waldhart et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2013.

claim: The S308A mutation loses an AMPK/Akt-phosphorylation site on Txnip.
source: An additional mutation, S308A, which loses an AMPK/Akt-phosphorylation site on Txnip (Waldhart et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2013), was tested in the context of WT Txnip and in the context of the C247S allele.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Waldhart et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2013.

claim: Txnip.S308A was not toxic to cones at P20 in rd1 mice.
source: In addition, the S308A allele was assayed for negative effects on cones by an assessment of rd1 cone number prior to P20, that is, before the onset of cone death (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C). It did not reduce the cone number at this early timepoint, indicating that Txnip.S308A was not toxic to cones.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The S308 residue is critical for the therapeutic function of Txnip.
source: This finding suggests that the S308 residue is critical for the therapeutic function of Txnip through an unclear mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that S308A mutation abolishes the therapeutic effect.

claim: Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA could still delay RP cone death compared to the control.
source: One additional set of amino acid changes, LL351 and 352AA, was tested in the context of C247S. This allele eliminates a clathrin-binding site, and thus hampers Txnip's ability to remove GLUT1 from cell surface through clathrin-coated pits (Wu et al., 2013). Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA could still delay RP cone death compared to the control (Figure 2B), suggesting that the therapeutic effect of Txnip was unlikely to be only through the removal of GLUT1 from the cell surface.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and citation to Wu et al., 2013.

claim: The LL351 and 352AA mutations eliminate a clathrin-binding site on Txnip.
source: One additional set of amino acid changes, LL351 and 352AA, was tested in the context of C247S. This allele eliminates a clathrin-binding site, and thus hampers Txnip's ability to remove GLUT1 from cell surface through clathrin-coated pits (Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2013.

claim: The therapeutic effect of Txnip was unlikely to be only through the removal of GLUT1 from the cell surface.
source: Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA could still delay RP cone death compared to the control (Figure 2B), suggesting that the therapeutic effect of Txnip was unlikely to be only through the removal of GLUT1 from the cell surface.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the LL351 and 352AA mutant, which cannot efficiently remove GLUT1, still provides cone rescue.

claim: An shRNA to Slc2a1 did not prolong RP cone survival.
source: To further explore the role of GLUT1, an shRNA to Slc2a1, which encodes GLUT1, was tested. It did not prolong RP cone survival (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: People with Txnip null mutations present with lactic acidosis.
source: People with Txnip null mutations present with lactic acidosis (Katsu-Jiménez et al., 2019), suggesting that Txnip deficiency might compromise lactate catabolism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Katsu-Jiménez et al., 2019.

claim: Txnip deficiency might compromise lactate catabolism.
source: People with Txnip null mutations present with lactic acidosis (Katsu-Jiménez et al., 2019), suggesting that Txnip deficiency might compromise lactate catabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Txnip null mutations cause lactic acidosis.

claim: A metabolomic study of muscle using a targeted knockout of Txnip suggested that Txnip increases the catabolism of non-glucose fuels.
source: A metabolomic study of muscle using a targeted knockout of Txnip suggested that Txnip increases the catabolism of non-glucose fuels, such as lactate, ketone bodies, and lipids (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to DeBalsi et al., 2014.

claim: Txnip increases the catabolism of lactate, ketone bodies, and lipids.
source: A metabolomic study of muscle using a targeted knockout of Txnip suggested that Txnip increases the catabolism of non-glucose fuels, such as lactate, ketone bodies, and lipids (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to DeBalsi et al., 2014.

claim: The switch in fuel preference by Txnip was proposed to benefit the mitochondrial TCA cycle, leading to greater production of ATP.
source: This switch in fuel preference was proposed to benefit the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA cycle), leading to a greater production of ATP.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on metabolomic data from DeBalsi et al., 2014.

claim: A problem for cones in the RP environment might be a shortage of glucose.
source: As presented earlier, a problem for cones in the RP environment might be a shortage of glucose (Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aït-Ali et al., 2015; Punzo et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2016.

claim: Txnip rescue was significantly decreased by any one of three Ldhb shRNAs.
source: We found that Txnip rescue was significantly decreased by any one of three Ldhb shRNAs (siLdhb) or by overexpression of Ldha (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: Txnip rescue was significantly decreased by overexpression of Ldha.
source: We found that Txnip rescue was significantly decreased by any one of three Ldhb shRNAs (siLdhb) or by overexpression of Ldha (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: Ldha converts pyruvate to lactate.
source: Ldhb, encoded by the Ldhb gene, is the enzyme that converts lactate to pyruvate to potentially fuel the TCA cycle, and lactate dehydrogenase a (Ldha, encoded by Ldha gene) converts pyruvate to lactate (Eventoff et al., 1977).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge supported by citation to Eventoff et al., 1977.

claim: shRNAs against Oxct1 or Cpt1a, tested singly or in combination, did not reduce the effectiveness of Txnip rescue.
source: We also tested the rescue effect of Txnip plus an shRNA against Oxct1 (siOxct1), a critical enzyme for ketolysis (Zhang and Xie, 2017), or against Cpt1a (siCpt1a), a component for lipid transporter that is rate limiting for β-oxidation (Shriver and Manchester, 2011). These shRNAs, tested singly or in combination, did not reduce the effectiveness of Txnip rescue (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and citations to Zhang and Xie, 2017; Shriver and Manchester, 2011.

claim: Oxct1 is a critical enzyme for ketolysis.
source: We also tested the rescue effect of Txnip plus an shRNA against Oxct1 (siOxct1), a critical enzyme for ketolysis (Zhang and Xie, 2017), or against Cpt1a (siCpt1a), a component for lipid transporter that is rate limiting for β-oxidation (Shriver and Manchester, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang and Xie, 2017.

claim: Cpt1a is a component for lipid transporter that is rate limiting for β-oxidation.
source: We also tested the rescue effect of Txnip plus an shRNA against Oxct1 (siOxct1), a critical enzyme for ketolysis (Zhang and Xie, 2017), or against Cpt1a (siCpt1a), a component for lipid transporter that is rate limiting for β-oxidation (Shriver and Manchester, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shriver and Manchester, 2011.

claim: The use of lactate, but not ketones or lipids, is critical as an alternative fuel for cones when Txnip is overexpressed.
source: Taken together, these data support the use of lactate, but not ketones or lipids, as a critical alternative fuel for cones when Txnip is overexpressed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ldhb knockdown reduces Txnip rescue, while Oxct1 and Cpt1a knockdown do not.

claim: Txnip increased the ATP:ADP ratio of rd1 cones in lactate-only medium.
source: Txnip increased the ATP:ADP ratio (i.e., higher FPercevalHR488:405) of rd1 cones in lactate-only medium.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: Txnip increased the ATP:ADP ratio of rd1 cones in pyruvate-only medium.
source: This was also seen in pyruvate-only medium, perhaps due to improved mitochondrial health (i.e., greater oxidative phosphorylation [OXPHOS] activity).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: Txnip-transduced cones had a lower ATP:ADP ratio in high-glucose medium.
source: Consistent with the role of Txnip in removing GLUT1 from the plasma membrane, Txnip-transduced cones had a lower ATP:ADP ratio (i.e., lower FPercevalHR488:405) in high-glucose medium (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: Intracellular glucose was reduced after overexpression of Txnip.
source: To further probe whether intracellular glucose was reduced after overexpression of Txnip (Wu et al., 2013), a glucose sensor iGlucoSnFR was used (Keller et al., 2019). This sensor showed reduced intracellular glucose in Txnip-transduced cones (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B and citations to Wu et al., 2013; Keller et al., 2019.

claim: There was no significant pH change in Txnip-transduced cones.
source: Because the fluorescence of GEFS may also be subject to environmental pH, we used a pH sensor, pHRed (Tantama et al., 2011), to determine if the changes of PercevalHR and iGlucoseSnFR were due to a change in pH, and found no significant pH change (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D and citation to Tantama et al., 2011.

claim: Lactate utilization by Txnip-transduced cones was critically dependent upon Ldhb for ATP production.
source: We also found that lactate, but not pyruvate, utilization by Txnip-transduced cones was critically dependent upon Ldhb for ATP production as introduction of siLdhb abrogated the increase in ATP:ADP in Txnip-transduced cones (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cones had a higher ATP:ADP ratio in lactate medium when Txnip.C247S was used relative to WT Txnip.
source: Furthermore, in correlation with improved cone survival by Txnip.C247S compared to WT Txnip (Figure 2B), cones had a higher ATP:ADP ratio in lactate medium when Txnip.C247S was used relative to WT Txnip (Figure 4D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D, E.

claim: There was no difference in the ATP:ADP ratio when Txnip.S308A was used, relative to control, in lactate medium.
source: Similarly, in correlation with no survival benefit when transduced with Txnip.S308A (Figure 2B), there was no difference in the ATP:ADP ratio when Txnip.S308A was used, relative to control, in lactate medium (Figure 4D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D, E.

claim: Three of the seven upregulated genes in Txnip-transduced RP cones were mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) genes.
source: By comparing the differentially expressed genes in common between the two strains, relative to control, 7 genes were seen to be upregulated and 17 were downregulated (Figure 5—source data 1). Three of the seven upregulated genes were mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) genes.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: The upregulation of three ETC genes in Txnip-transduced rd1 cones was confirmed by ddPCR.
source: The upregulation of these three ETC genes in Txnip-transduced rd1 cones was confirmed by ddPCR (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There was almost no Txnip mRNA detected by RNA-seq in the WT or RP control cones.
source: Interestingly, there was almost no Txnip mRNA detected by RNA-seq in the WT or RP control cones, but there was high number of Txnip transcripts following addition of RedO-Txnip in all strains (Figure 5—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—source data 3.

claim: There was a high number of Txnip transcripts following addition of RedO-Txnip in all strains.
source: Interestingly, there was almost no Txnip mRNA detected by RNA-seq in the WT or RP control cones, but there was high number of Txnip transcripts following addition of RedO-Txnip in all strains (Figure 5—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—source data 3.

claim: Cone mitochondria were swollen and deteriorated in rd10 mouse retinas.
source: Murakami et al. previously showed that cone mitochondria were swollen and deteriorated in rd10 mouse retinas (Murakami et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Murakami et al., 2012.

claim: There was an increase in the size of mitochondrial cross sections by Txnip transduction in P20 rd1 cones.
source: There was an increase in the size of mitochondrial cross sections by Txnip transduction, with a greater increase following transduction with Txnip.C247S in P20 rd1 cones (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: There was a greater increase in mitochondrial size following transduction with Txnip.C247S compared to WT Txnip in P20 rd1 cones.
source: There was an increase in the size of mitochondrial cross sections by Txnip transduction, with a greater increase following transduction with Txnip.C247S in P20 rd1 cones (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: Both Txnip and Txnip.C247S increased the ratio of J-aggregates:JC1-monomers in P20 rd1 cones.
source: Mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), a reflection of mitochondrial ETC function, was also examined using JC-1 dye staining of freshly explanted Txnip-transduced P20 rd1 retinas (Reers et al., 1995). Both Txnip and Txnip.C247S increased the ratio of J-aggregates:JC1-monomers (Figure 5C, D), indicating an increased ΔΨm and/or a greater number/size of mitochondria with a high ΔΨm following Txnip overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, D and citation to Reers et al., 1995.

claim: The increased J-aggregates:JC1-monomers ratio indicates an increased ΔΨm and/or a greater number/size of mitochondria with a high ΔΨm following Txnip overexpression.
source: Both Txnip and Txnip.C247S increased the ratio of J-aggregates:JC1-monomers (Figure 5C, D), indicating an increased ΔΨm and/or a greater number/size of mitochondria with a high ΔΨm following Txnip overexpression.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the JC-1 dye staining results based on established knowledge of JC-1 function.

claim: The intensity of mitoRFP was higher in P20 rd1 cones transduced with Txnip compared to control cones.
source: This finding was further investigated in vivo using infection by an AAV encoding mitoRFP, which only accumulates in mitochondria with a high ΔΨm (Brodier et al., 2020; Hood et al., 2003). Compared to the control cones without Txnip transduction, the intensity of mitoRFP was higher in P20 rd1 cones transduced with Txnip (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D and citations to Brodier et al., 2020; Hood et al., 2003.

claim: Parp1 can negatively affect mitochondria through deleterious effects on the mitochondrial genome.
source: Among these interactors was Parp1, which can negatively affect mitochondria through deleterious effects on the mitochondrial genome (Hocsak et al., 2017; Szczesny et al., 2014), as well as effects on inflammation and other cellular pathways (Fehr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hocsak et al., 2017; Szczesny et al., 2014.

claim: Parp1 has effects on inflammation and other cellular pathways.
source: Among these interactors was Parp1, which can negatively affect mitochondria through deleterious effects on the mitochondrial genome (Hocsak et al., 2017; Szczesny et al., 2014), as well as effects on inflammation and other cellular pathways (Fehr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fehr et al., 2020.

claim: Parp1 expression was enriched in cone inner segments and cone nuclei.
source: Parp1 expression was first examined by IHC and found to be enriched in cone inner segments, which are packed with mitochondria (Hoang et al., 2002), as well as in cone nuclei (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and citation to Hoang et al., 2002.

claim: Cone inner segments are packed with mitochondria.
source: Parp1 expression was first examined by IHC and found to be enriched in cone inner segments, which are packed with mitochondria (Hoang et al., 2002), as well as in cone nuclei (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hoang et al., 2002.

claim: Parp1-/- rd1 cones possessed larger mitochondria than Parp1+/+ rd1 cones.
source: To test for a role of Parp1, Parp1-/- mice were bred to rd1 mice, and their cone mitochondria were examined by TEM and mitoRFP. Parp1-/- rd1 cones possessed larger mitochondria (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H, I) and higher mitoRFP signals than cones from Parp1+/+ rd1 controls (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1H, I.

claim: Parp1-/- rd1 cones had higher mitoRFP signals than cones from Parp1+/+ rd1 controls.
source: To test for a role of Parp1, Parp1-/- mice were bred to rd1 mice, and their cone mitochondria were examined by TEM and mitoRFP. Parp1-/- rd1 cones possessed larger mitochondria (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H, I) and higher mitoRFP signals than cones from Parp1+/+ rd1 controls (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: Addition of Txnip.C247S to Parp1-/- rd1 cones did not alter the mitoRFP signals.
source: Addition of Txnip.C247S to Parp1-/- rd1 cones did not alter the mitoRFP signals (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: Txnip.C247S-mediated cone survival in Parp1-/- rd1 retinas was similar to that of Txnip.C247S-transduced Parp1+/+ rd1 retinas.
source: When Txnip.C247S was added to Parp1-/- rd1 retinas, cone survival was similar to that of Txnip.C247S-transduced Parp1+/+ rd1 retinas, showing that Txnip-mediated survival does not require Parp1 (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G, H.

claim: Txnip-mediated survival does not require Parp1.
source: When Txnip.C247S was added to Parp1-/- rd1 retinas, cone survival was similar to that of Txnip.C247S-transduced Parp1+/+ rd1 retinas, showing that Txnip-mediated survival does not require Parp1 (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Txnip rescue is similar in Parp1+/+ and Parp1-/- backgrounds.

claim: Parp1-/- rd1 cone survival was similar to Parp1+/+ rd1 cones.
source: Parp1-/- rd1 cone survival also was similar to the Parp1+/+ rd1 cones (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G, H.

claim: Mitochondrial improvement alone is not sufficient to prolong cone survival.
source: The discordance between improved mitochondria and cone survival in these experiments suggested that mitochondrial improvement alone is not sufficient to prolong cone survival.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Parp1-/- cones have healthier mitochondria but similar survival to Parp1+/+ cones.

claim: Txnip.S308A and Txnip + siLdhb both failed to prolong rd1 cone survival despite improvements in mitochondria.
source: This is consistent with the observations from transduction with Txnip.S308A, as well as Txnip + siLdhb, both of which failed to prolong rd1 cone survival despite improvements in mitochondria (Figure 2A, B, Figure 5A–D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, B, Figure 5A–D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Ldhb alone did not prolong cone survival in Parp1+/+ rd1 mice.
source: To test if improved cone survival requires enhanced lactate catabolism in addition to mitochondrial improvement, we delivered Ldhb to Parp1-/- rd1 cones. Unlike on Parp1+/+ background (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D), a small but significant improvement in cone survival was observed (Figure 5I, J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ldhb delivery to Parp1-/- rd1 cones resulted in a small but significant improvement in cone survival.
source: To test if improved cone survival requires enhanced lactate catabolism in addition to mitochondrial improvement, we delivered Ldhb to Parp1-/- rd1 cones. Unlike on Parp1+/+ background (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D), a small but significant improvement in cone survival was observed (Figure 5I, J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5I, J.

claim: Cone photoreceptors require high levels of ATP to maintain their membrane potential, relying primarily upon the Na+/K+ ATPase pump.
source: Cone photoreceptors are known to require high levels of ATP to maintain their membrane potential, relying primarily upon the Na+/K+ ATPase pump (Ingram et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ingram et al., 2020.

claim: Addition of Txnip improved Na+/K+ pump function of P20 rd1 cones in lactate medium.
source: To investigate whether Txnip affects the function of the Na+/K+ pump in RP cones, freshly explanted P20 rd1 retinas were stained with RH421, a fluorescent small-molecule probe for Na+/K+ pump function (Fedosova et al., 1995). Addition of Txnip improved Na+/K+ pump function of these cones in lactate medium as reflected by an increase in RH421 fluorescence (Figure 6A, B), consistent with Txnip enabling greater utilization of lactate as fuel.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A, B and citation to Fedosova et al., 1995.

claim: Protein expression of cone opsin is downregulated in RP cones, postulated to be due to insufficient energy supply.
source: In RP cones, it is also known that protein expression of cone opsin is downregulated, postulated to be due to insufficient energy supply (Punzo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Punzo et al., 2009.

claim: Greater anti-opsin staining was observed in Txnip-transduced rd1 cones at P50 compared to control.
source: Compared to control, greater anti-opsin staining was observed in Txnip-transduced rd1 cones at P50 (Figure 6C), further supporting the idea that Txnip improves the energy supply to RP cones.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: HIF1α can upregulate the transcription of glycolytic genes.
source: HIF1α can upregulate the transcription of glycolytic genes (Majmundar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Majmundar et al., 2010.

claim: Dominant-negative HIF1α (dnHIF1α) increased rd1 cone survival.
source: To investigate whether HIF1α might play a role in cone survival, a WT and a dominant-negative HIF1α (dnHIF1α) allele (Jiang et al., 1996) were delivered to rd1 retinas using AAV. A target gene of HIF1α, Vegfa, which might improve blood flow and thus nutrient delivery (but might also increase inflammation), also was tested. The dnHIF1α increased rd1 cone survival, while WT Hif1a and Vegf each decreased cone survival (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7 and citation to Jiang et al., 1996.

claim: WT Hif1a decreased rd1 cone survival.
source: The dnHIF1α increased rd1 cone survival, while WT Hif1a and Vegf each decreased cone survival (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Vegf decreased rd1 cone survival.
source: The dnHIF1α increased rd1 cone survival, while WT Hif1a and Vegf each decreased cone survival (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: AAV-Best1-Txnip.LL351 and 352AA resulted in less clearance of GLUT1 from the surface of the RPE relative to WT Txnip.
source: To examine the level of GLUT1 in the RPE following introduction of WT Txnip, or Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA, which should prevent efficient removal of GLUT1 (see background in previous section), IHC for GLUT1 was carried out. This assay showed that AAV-Best1-Txnip.LL351 and 352AA did result in less clearance of GLUT1 from the surface of the RPE relative to WT Txnip (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA improved rd1 cone survival.
source: Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA was then tested for rd1 cone rescue, where it was found to improve cone survival (Figure 7), in keeping with the model that the RPE retains glucose to the detriment of cones in RP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The RPE retains glucose to the detriment of cones in RP.
source: Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA was then tested for rd1 cone rescue, where it was found to improve cone survival (Figure 7), in keeping with the model that the RPE retains glucose to the detriment of cones in RP.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the observation that preventing GLUT1 removal from RPE improves cone survival.

claim: The combination of Txnip.C247S expression in cones with expression of Nrf2 in the RPE provided an additive effect on cone survival relative to either gene alone.
source: The combination of Txnip.C247S expression in cones, with expression of Nrf2, a gene with anti-oxidative damage and anti-inflammatory activity, in the RPE, provided an additive effect on cone survival relative to either gene alone (Figure 8A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A, B.

claim: The combination of RedO-Txnip.C247S and Best1-Nrf2 led to the localization of opsin protein to the outer segment-like structure, rather than to the plasma membrane.
source: The combination of RedO-Txnip.C247S and Best1-Nrf2 led to the localization of opsin protein to the outer segment-like structure, rather than to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In WT cones, opsin protein is localized to the outer segment.
source: In WT cones, opsin protein is localized to the outer segment, where photon detection and phototransduction take place.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cone opsin localization.

claim: During degeneration in RP, the cone outer segments collapse, and opsin is mislocalized to the plasma membrane.
source: During degeneration in RP, the cone outer segments collapse, and opsin is mislocalized to the plasma membrane (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AAV-Best1-Nrf2 alone suppressed the formation of craters in FVB rd1 retinas.
source: An additional morphological phenotype that is especially prominent in the FVB rd1 strain is that of 'craters' in the photoreceptor layer. These are circumscribed areas without cones that are obvious when the retina is viewed as a flat-mount. AAV-Best1-Nrf2 alone suppressed the formation of these craters (Figure 8A; Wu et al., 2021), while AAV-RedO-Txnip did not, despite the fact that AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S provided the most robust RP cone rescue (Figure 2A, Figure 8A, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and citation to Wu et al., 2021.

claim: AAV-RedO-Txnip did not suppress the formation of craters in FVB rd1 retinas.
source: AAV-Best1-Nrf2 alone suppressed the formation of these craters (Figure 8A; Wu et al., 2021), while AAV-RedO-Txnip did not, despite the fact that AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S provided the most robust RP cone rescue (Figure 2A, Figure 8A, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: dnHIF1α decreased the FVB-specific retinal craters.
source: It was also noted that dnHIF1α decreased, and Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA increased, the FVB-specific retinal craters, while both vectors prolonged RP cone survival (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA increased the FVB-specific retinal craters.
source: It was also noted that dnHIF1α decreased, and Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA increased, the FVB-specific retinal craters, while both vectors prolonged RP cone survival (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The combination of AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S with AAV-RedO-Tgfb1 did not improve cone survival beyond that of Txnip alone.
source: An additional combination that was tested was AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S with AAV-RedO-Tgfb1, an anti-inflammatory gene that our previous studies showed could eliminate the craters on its own (Wang et al., 2020). This combination did not improve cone survival beyond that of Txnip alone, but almost completely eliminated the craters in an additive fashion with Txnip (Figure 8D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D, E and citation to Wang et al., 2020.

claim: The combination of AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S with AAV-RedO-Tgfb1 almost completely eliminated the craters in an additive fashion.
source: This combination did not improve cone survival beyond that of Txnip alone, but almost completely eliminated the craters in an additive fashion with Txnip (Figure 8D, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D, E.

claim: Tgfb1 is an anti-inflammatory gene that could eliminate the craters on its own.
source: An additional combination that was tested was AAV-RedO-Txnip.C247S with AAV-RedO-Tgfb1, an anti-inflammatory gene that our previous studies showed could eliminate the craters on its own (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2020.

claim: Other genes (Hk2, Ldhb, and Cx3cl1) and Nrf2 expressed specifically in cones in combination with WT Txnip did not provide any obvious improvement over Txnip alone.
source: In addition, other genes (Hk2, Ldhb, and Cx3cl1) and Nrf2 were expressed specifically in cones in combination with WT Txnip, but did not provide any obvious improvement over Txnip alone (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Photoreceptors have been characterized as being highly glycolytic, even under aerobic conditions.
source: Photoreceptors have been characterized as being highly glycolytic, even under aerobic conditions, as originally described by Warburg, 1925.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Warburg, 1925.

claim: Glucose appears to be supplied primarily from the circulation, via the RPE, which has a high level of GLUT1.
source: Glucose appears to be supplied primarily from the circulation, via the RPE, which has a high level of GLUT1 (Gospe et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gospe et al., 2010.

claim: Photoreceptors, at least rods, carry out glycolysis to support anabolism, to replace their outer segments.
source: Photoreceptors, at least rods, carry out glycolysis to support anabolism, to replace their outer segments (Chinchore et al., 2017), and contribute ATP, to run their ion pumps (Okawa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chinchore et al., 2017.

claim: Photoreceptors carry out glycolysis to contribute ATP to run their ion pumps.
source: Photoreceptors, at least rods, carry out glycolysis to support anabolism, to replace their outer segments (Chinchore et al., 2017), and contribute ATP, to run their ion pumps (Okawa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okawa et al., 2008.

claim: If glucose becomes limited in RP, cones may have insufficient fuel for their needs.
source: If glucose becomes limited, as has been proposed to occur in RP, cones may have insufficient fuel for their needs.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the glucose shortage hypothesis.

claim: The Txnip.C247S allele prevents binding to thioredoxins and gave enhanced cone survival relative to WT Txnip.
source: The Txnip.C247S allele prevents binding to thioredoxins and gave enhanced cone survival relative to WT Txnip (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: By being free of the thioredoxin interaction, the C247S mutant protein may be more available for other Txnip-mediated activities.
source: We speculate that, by being free of this interaction, the C247S mutant protein may be more available for other Txnip-mediated activities.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of C247S enhanced activity.

claim: Thioredoxin may be made more available for its role in fighting oxidative damage following transduction of the C247S mutant, rather than the WT Txnip allele.
source: In addition, thioredoxin may be made more available for its role in fighting oxidative damage following transduction of the C247S mutant, rather than the WT Txnip allele.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of C247S enhanced activity.

claim: A study of Txnip's function in skeletal muscle suggested that it plays a role in fuel selection.
source: The mechanisms by which Txnip might benefit cones are not fully known, but a study of Txnip's function in skeletal muscle suggested that it plays a role in fuel selection (DeBalsi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to DeBalsi et al., 2014.

claim: Cones express Oxct1 mRNA, suggesting that cones are capable of ketolysis.
source: Cones express oOxct1 mRNA (Shekhar et al., 2016), which encodes a critical enzyme for ketone catabolism, suggesting that cones are capable of ketolysis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shekhar et al., 2016.

claim: A previous study showed that lipids might be an alternative energy source for cones by β-oxidation.
source: In addition, a previous study showed that lipids might be an alternative energy source for cones by β-oxidation (Joyal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Joyal et al., 2016.

claim: Cones can use alternative fuels to meet their intense energy demands.
source: It is likely that cones can use these alternative fuels to meet their intense energy demands (Ingram et al., 2020; Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ingram et al., 2020 and experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Txnip rescue did not depend on ketolysis or β-oxidation.
source: However, the Txnip rescue did not depend on ketolysis or β-oxidation (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Photoreceptors normally have high levels of Ldha.
source: This is an interesting switch as photoreceptors normally have high levels of Ldha (Figure 5—source data 4) and produce lactate (Chinchore et al., 2017; Kanow et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—source data 4 and citations to Chinchore et al., 2017; Kanow et al., 2017.

claim: Photoreceptors normally produce lactate.
source: This is an interesting switch as photoreceptors normally have high levels of Ldha (Figure 5—source data 4) and produce lactate (Chinchore et al., 2017; Kanow et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chinchore et al., 2017; Kanow et al., 2017.

claim: Lactate is highly available from serum.
source: An important factor in the reliance on Ldhb could be the availability of lactate, which is highly available from serum (Hui et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hui et al., 2017.

claim: Ketones are usually only available during fasting.
source: Ketones are usually only available during fasting, and lipids are hydrophobic molecules that are slow to be transported across the plasma membranes.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about ketone availability.

claim: Lipids are hydrophobic molecules that are slow to be transported across the plasma membranes.
source: Ketones are usually only available during fasting, and lipids are hydrophobic molecules that are slow to be transported across the plasma membranes.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about lipid transport.

claim: Lipids are required to rebuild the membrane-rich outer segments.
source: Moreover, lipids are required to rebuild the membrane-rich outer segments, and thus might be somewhat limited.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the structure of outer segments.

claim: Ldhb is not sufficient to delay RP cone degeneration.
source: Ldhb is not sufficient, however, to delay RP cone degeneration as its overexpression did not promote RP cone survival.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Txnip-transduced RP cones had larger mitochondria with a greater membrane potential.
source: Txnip-transduced RP cones also had larger mitochondria with a greater membrane potential and likely were able to use the pyruvate produced by Ldhb for greater ATP production via OXPHOS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Txnip-transduced cones likely were able to use the pyruvate produced by Ldhb for greater ATP production via OXPHOS.
source: Txnip-transduced RP cones also had larger mitochondria with a greater membrane potential and likely were able to use the pyruvate produced by Ldhb for greater ATP production via OXPHOS.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the observed increase in ATP:ADP ratio and mitochondrial health.

claim: Txnip-transduced cones had an enhanced ATP:ADP ratio.
source: Indeed, Txnip-transduced cones had an enhanced ATP:ADP ratio (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Healthier mitochondria were not sufficient to prolong RP cone survival.
source: However, healthier mitochondria were not sufficient to prolong RP cone survival.
